title: Random Quantum LDPC Codes Approaching the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound
authors: Tushant Mittal, Shashank Srivastava, Madhur Tulsiani, Mary Wootters
abstract: We show that for any $R,ε>0$ and any prime $p\geq 2$, there exists an infinite family of $p$-ary quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, rate $R$, checks of weight $O_ε(1)$, and normalized distance at least $δ_{\mathrm{GV}}(p,R)-ε$. Here, $δ_{\mathrm{GV}}(p,R)$ denotes the quantum Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound for $p$-ary stabilizer codes.   In fact, we construct an ensemble of such QLDPC codes, such that a random code from this ensemble is close to the GV bound with high probability. Moreover, this ensemble matches the performance of random stabilizer codes on several quantum channels. Specifically, it approaches the quantum capacity of the erasure channel and the hashing bound for memoryless Pauli channels, including the depolarizing channel.   A significant challenge in working with QLDPC codes is that they are necessarily \emph{degenerate}, i.e., contain many low-weight stabilizers. A key contribution of our work is a construction of QLDPC codes with quantitative control on their degeneracy. These codes are obtained by combining known constructions of asymptotically good QLDPC codes with the expander-based distance amplification procedure of Alon, Edmonds, and Luby [FOCS'95].   Our random ensemble is constructed by starting with these low-degeneracy QLDPC codes near the quantum Singleton bound and concatenating each coordinate with a random inner code. This can be viewed as a quantum analogue of Thommesen's construction, and as an LDPC version of a result of Ouyang, with an appropriately designed outer code.
summary: This paper constructs an infinite family of Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes that provably approach the quantum Gilbert-Varshamov bound. By addressing the challenge of code degeneracy, the authors show that these codes can match the performance of random stabilizer codes across various quantum channels. This advances the practical design of high-rate, good-distance quantum error-correcting codes.
main_problem: To prove that Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes can achieve the quantum Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound, and to show that random QLDPC ensembles match the performance of random stabilizer codes on various quantum channels.
main_result: The authors construct an ensemble of QLDPC codes such that a random code approaches the quantum GV bound with high probability, matching the performance of random stabilizer codes for channels like the erasure and depolarizing channels.
method: The construction involves combining low-degeneracy QLDPC codes (obtained via the Alon, Edmonds, and Luby distance amplification procedure) with random inner codes via concatenation, viewed as a quantum analogue of Thommesen's construction.
model_or_system: The work focuses on quantum stabilizer codes, specifically QLDPC codes defined by row-sparse parity-check matrices. The analysis is conducted using the linear-algebraic formulation of stabilizer spaces.
key_observables: Rate ($R$), relative distance ($\delta$), and the quantum Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound ($\delta_{GV}(p, R)$).
important_parameters: The alphabet size $p$, the degeneracy parameter $\eta$, and the error tolerance $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the ability to control the degeneracy of the QLDPC codes using the AEL procedure, which is necessary because QLDPC codes are inherently degenerate.

paper_structure: The paper develops by first establishing the need to control degeneracy, then detailing the AEL construction to achieve low-degeneracy outer codes approaching the quantum Singleton bound, and finally combining this with random inner codes to prove the overall approach to the GV bound.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, constructive methods for designing quantum error-correcting codes (QEC) that approach fundamental theoretical limits (like the GV bound), which is central to fault-tolerant quantum computation.
